items.title: Until Dawn 2 Reveals Release Date in New Trailer
items.description: Until Dawn 2 will release on PS5 this January, as confirmed by a new trailer for the game.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Until Dawn 2 will release on PS5 this January, as confirmed by a new trailer for the game.

During today's PlayStation State of Play, Firesprite showed off a new look at Until Dawn 2. The trailer teases the franchise's signature branching narrative with deadly choices that can radically change the fate of your characters. However, the biggest takeaway is that the game is coming out very soon, much sooner than some of us could have expected.

Until Dawn 2 will release on January 28, 2027 with pre-orders opening on September 10.

Today's announcement comes as part of the latest showcase from PlayStation. Catch up on everything announced during Sony's State of Play September 2026 broadcast right here.

items.title: Crimson Desert's First Expansion Is Releasing Next Month
items.description: Crimson Desert's first expansion releases in October, and it's going to have a ton of game-changing content, including underwater gameplay.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Crimson Desert's first expansion releases in October, and it's going to have a ton of game-changing content, including underwater gameplay.

During today's PlayStation State of Play, Pearl Abyss announced Crimson Desert: Chartering the Unknown, a brand new expansion for one of 2026's breakout titles. The new DLC will release on October 15 and add city building mechanics, underwater exploration, a ship that players can captain, and much more. The DLC takes place after the main story and continues the story of the game, so players should probably go back and finish the game if they haven't already to prepare for the new DLC.

As of right now, we're not sure how much this expansion will cost, but it certainly won't be free. Those who pre-order will get a free deep sea diver outfit as a nice bonus. If you were already feeling overwhelmed by all the games coming out in September and October, Pearl Abyss is ensuring you'll have something else to sink dozens of hours into.

Crimson Desert debuted earlier this year and immediately became one of the biggest games of 2026. Players were fond off the game's deep open-world RPG mechanics, allowing for nuanced and rich combat and exploration. It's a game that you can sink countless hours into without getting bored, so it's great to see Pearl Abyss is keeping players well-fed so soon after release.

Today's announcement comes as part of the latest showcase from PlayStation. Catch up on everything announced during Sony's State of Play September 2026 broadcast right here.

items.title: Double Fine Shadow Drops Former Xbox Console Exclusive Keeper on PlayStation 5 Today
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Double Fine has wasted no time in bringing its curious adventure game Keeper to PlayStation 5, just weeks after the studio was ditched by Xbox.

Keeper is a colorful and dreamy adventure starring a crumbling lighthouse and a mysterious bird. Despite being critically praised, the project failed to find a wide audience on Xbox Series X/S and PC where it debuted last year, and was Double Fine's penultimate project before Microsoft decided to cut ties with the company.

Its arrival on PlayStation isn't a huge surprise — Double Fine has brought other titles to PS5 as well during its now-concluded era of Xbox ownership — though its swift arrival is still notable. Likewise, the fact that this news was confirmed today in Sony's big State of Play broadcast — it's harder to imagine the news appearing in this way had the studio remained under Xbox's thumb.

"Exploring Keeper’s surreal world is a feast for the senses, with every detail from its propulsive score to its Seussian flora and fauna pulling me deeper into its tale," we wrote in IGN's Keeper review, awarding it a 9/10 score.

Earlier this week, Double Fine launched a new Kickstarter campaign to help secure its immediate future, and promised to make Brütal Legend 2 if it raised an impossible-sounding $100 million.

Today's announcement comes as part of the latest showcase from PlayStation. Catch up on everything announced during Sony's State of Play September 2026 broadcast right here.

items.title: Ghost of Yōtei is Getting a Roguelike Survival Mode That Includes Ghost of Tsushima's Jin
items.description: PlayStation blockbuster Ghost of Yotei is getting a new single-player roguelike mode, Most Wanted, as part of its Complete Edition that includes upcoming expansion Echoes of Sekigahara.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
PlayStation blockbuster Ghost of Yōtei is getting a new single-player roguelike mode, Most Wanted, as part of its Complete Edition that includes its upcoming expansion Echoes of Sekigahara.

Take down Most Wanted targets within the mode and you'll progress through tougher fights using various modifiers, and ultimately unlock more characters — including Ghost of Tsushima's Jin Sakai, who arrives with all four of his signature stances.

As well as Atsu, Oyuki and Nagato will also be playable, before you unlock Jin.

"For Jin, our animation and character art teams worked hard to take his Ghost of Tsushima model and keep it faithful while also applying upgrades for Ghost of Yōtei," wrote Sucker Punch Productions' Andrew Goldfarb. "Jin can use his katana with all four of the original stances from Ghost of Tsushima, helping to exploit enemy weaknesses. He also starts with a Sticky Bomb and hankyu.

"Jin’s Ultimate is the Dance of Wrath skill from Ghost of Tsushima, which targets multiple enemies and disarms them, and his Kill Streak is, of course, Ghost Stance, which allows him to terrify the enemies around him and kill a limited amount of them in a single hit."

All of this will launch on October 1, the same date previously announced for Echoes of Sekigahara. Existing owners of the game can upgrade for $14.99, or alternatively you can purchase Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition digitally now for $69.99, with new content unlocking on October 1.

Today's announcement comes as part of the latest showcase from PlayStation. Catch up on everything announced during Sony's State of Play September 2026 broadcast right here.

items.title: Marvel Will Reveal The Truth About That Deadpool & Wolverine's Crying Hulk Flashforward, Ryan Reynolds Promises
items.description: Ryan Reynolds has promised that Marvel will reveal the truth behind Deadpool & Wolverine's mysterious flashforward with Thor — eventually, at least.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Ryan Reynolds has promised that Marvel will reveal the truth behind that mysterious Deadpool & Wolverine flashforward featuring Thor — eventually, at least.

Interviewed by Entertainment Today, Reynolds was asked about the curious moment in his hugely successful Wolverine team-up movie where Deadpool appears to glimpse a future version of himself lying gravely injured, while Chris Hemsworth's Thor looks tearfully on.

"Don't we all want to know why was Thor crying? I want to know too," Reynolds teased. "We will find out at some point. And I'm excited for people to find out."

Could the moment be coming in Avengers: Doomsday or Avengers: Secret Wars? Here, Reynolds appeared to plead complete ignorance of his potential role in either film, despite having appeared at both San Diego Comic-Con and D23 this summer to help promote the movie.

Asked about his recent humorous appearance with Hugh Jackman where the two stars appeared to beg for a role in Doomsday, Reynolds said he "still didn't know" what that clip meant (this seems extremely unlikely) and that there was "a lot to unpack" in it (there really was not).

Reynolds' involvement in Doomsday was stated last year by The Hollywood Reporter, so there's really no question around whether he will actually turn up. So far, however, Marvel appears to be keeping its focus on promoting Doomsday with the movies (many) major players: the Avengers, New Avengers, Fantastic Four and X-Men.

Earlier this week, Avengers: Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo defended shooting the film without a finished script, stating that their improvisational style of production was where "the magic happened."

Image credit: Marvel/YouTube

items.title: People Are Spamming Sony's State of Play Chat With Destiny 3 Requests
items.description: Destiny fans are spamming Sony’s State of Play livestream chat with the hashtag #WeWantDestiny, as they continue to call for more from Bungie’s looter shooter franchise, including Destiny 3.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Destiny fans are spamming Sony’s State of Play livestream chat with the hashtag #WeWantDestiny, as they continue to call for more from Bungie’s looter shooter franchise, including Destiny 3.

At the time of this article’s publication, with 15 minutes until today’s State of Play (check out our live blog here for all the announcements), chat across various livestreams was packed with #WeWantDestiny as well as calls for Destiny 3, as fans continue to push for a continuation of the series.

Bungie walked away from Destiny 2 earlier this year, with parent company Sony backing a focus on struggling extraction shooter Marathon instead. However, various Marathon updates have failed to kickstart the game, leading to ever louder calls for a return to Destiny.

Despite the focal support for Destiny 3, it seems unlikely that Sony will green light the game, which would surely be yet another risky expensive development project at a time of extreme caution across the video game industry. But could Bungie have more Destiny in some shape or form in the works? With Marathon struggling for player numbers, how long will Sony give it before the axe falls on that game, too?

Bungie's issues with Destiny 2 reportedly began around the time of last summer's Edge of Fate expansion, which was said to have underperformed. The decision to pull the plug was allegedly made "earlier this year" after it was decided not to relaunch the franchise as "Destiny Infinity."

Forbes reported that Bungie began discussing different scenarios about "what the future of Destiny 2 would look like" after December's Renegades, its Star Wars-themed crossover expansion, "did even worse [than Edge of Fate] and didn't change sales or retention trajectory."

Destiny Infinity would have been a relaunch alongside a return to the one big expansion model Destiny used to have, but the idea fell by the wayside after it was allegedly decided that the costs and risks were too high, especially in the context of support for Marathon.

Destiny 3 "was considered, as ever, but things didn't swing that way," and there has been no behind-the-scenes hints that a third Destiny game is coming, with the cost of the game's production cited as the key issue.

Destiny 2 launched on PlayStation 4 and Xbox One on September 6, 2017, with a PC version following a month later. Behind the scenes, however, tension between Bungie and publisher Activision emerged, and the two companies officially parted ways in January 2019, ending their 10-year publishing deal five years early.

With Destiny in its own hands, Bungie self-published the game, but it couldn't escape financial troubles and layoffs as Destiny 2 expansions failed to hit the mark and the player base dwindled. Extraction shooter Marathon launched early March, with a reported budget of more than $250 million. It too, according to analysts, has failed to meet sales expectations.

Bungie has struggled financially for some time, and reportedly was on the brink of closure before Sony bought the studio back in 2022 for $3.6 billion. Sony recently reported a $765 million impairment loss due to underperformance of Bungie specifically.

Bungie suffered a significant round of layoffs that came with the decision to end Destiny 2 development. The cuts hit nearly 300 staff who worked at the developer’s Bellevue, Washington office, official records revealed.

A Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) notice issued by Sony to the Washington State Employment Security Department, reported by Game File, revealed 292 staff had been let go with a formal separation date set for July 9. This number does not account for Bungie staff outside Washington state. It is unknown how many staff remain at Bungie following the cuts, although the studio was reported to have employed 850 staff as of 2024.

It was Bungie's third round of layoffs in three years. According to The Seattle Times, Bungie once had 1,000 employees in Bellevue, according to a 2023 annual financial report from the city. Between October 2023 and July 2024, Bungie laid off around 320 staff. Local press called the cuts a "bloodbath."

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: LIVE: State of Play September 2026 — All the Gameplay, Trailers, and Announcements
items.description: It’s State of Play time, and IGN will be reporting live on all the gameplay reveals, trailers, and announcements as they happen right here in our live blog.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
It’s State of Play time, and IGN will be reporting live on all the gameplay reveals, trailers, and announcements as they happen right here in our live blog. The action kicks off on September 3 starting at 6am PT / 9am ET / 2pm UK / 3pm CEST / 10pm JST.

Sony has two State of Play broadcasts set for today airing back-to-back (IGN will be carrying the stream). The first is a new State of Play that features updates and announcements from PlayStation Studios and third-party partners. It concludes with an extended look at Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy ender, Revelation.

Right after that, we’ll get a new State of Play Japan, which focuses on games from studios in Japan and Asia. Expect new gameplay, announcements, and more from that one.

We’ve got a What to Expect From PlayStation’s State of Play September 2026 article packed with our speculation live now, but my feeling is that Naughty Dog’s Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet may end up being the star of the show. It’s been some time since we’ve seen the game, so a September State of Play feels like an appropriate venue for an update.

Elsewhere, there are a number of PlayStation Studios that have been quiet for some time now. Dreams and LittleBigPlanet developer Media Molecule is among them, as is Days Gone developer Bend Studio. Will we see Firesprite’s Until Dawn 2? And what about Haven Studios’ Fairgame? Sony’s live service ambition has fallen apart, but the last time I checked, Fairgame was still alive.

Check back right here to find out what PlayStation has in store for fans. I'll be live blogging the event via updates below.

That's the end of State of Play, but we have more from State of Play Japan...

State of Play ended with the extended look at Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which means no Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet update from Naughty Dog. Other no-shows included Media Molecule, Sony Bend, and Haven Studio's Fairgame.

Final Fantasy VII Revelation release date

Final Fantasy VII Revelation ends the remake trilogy on April 8, 2027. State of Play delivered a new trailer and 10 minutes of fresh gameplay footage.

GTA 6 Dualsense controller

GTA 6 featured in State of Play via a DualSense controller. That Rockstar / PlayStation partnership is certainly putting in work! Two new limited edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by GTA 6 are in the works: DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI Black Limited Edition; and DualSense Wireless Controller – Grand Theft Auto VI White Limited Edition.

Both limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers launch on November 19 priced $84.99 USD/ ¥12,480 (including tax) / €84.99/ £74.99. Pre-orders start September 10 at 10am local time.

Until Dawn 2

Firesprite's Until Dawn 2 got a new trailer at State of Play. The impressive character models feature realistic faces in various states of terror. It hits PS5 on January 26, 2027.

Gran Turismo 7 update

Gran Turismo 7 is getting a big update. Creator Kazunori Yamauchi hit State of Play to reveal all the details, with the Spec IV Update releasing by the end of year in two parts (October and December).

Saros update

Housemarque's Saros is getting a free update called Zenith.

PS Plus updates

Mega Man X: Command Mission, Dino Crisis 2, and the original Ratchet & Clank hit the PlayStation Plus Classics Catalog over the course of the rest of 2026. Dino Crisis 2 is certainly an interesting one, amid calls from fans for a brand new sequel in the survival horror series. Launching into Game Catalog is Pigeons at Play's Mycopunk.

Rhapsody in Scarlet

More from Konami: Rhapsody in Scarlet.

Rev.Noir

We got a new look at Konami's upcoming RPG Rev.Noir running on PS5 Pro. It's due out next year.

3 indie games coming to PlayStation

State of Play introduced three new indie games coming to PlayStation: Hunter's Moon; Annapurna's Uncanyon; and Double Fine's Keeper, which is available on PS5 today following the studio's independence from Microsoft ownership.

Gundam Rogue Orbit

Gundam Rogue Orbit got a new trailer, and confirmation of a release date: March 5, 2027.

Final Fantasy Resonance

Square Enix announced a demo for Final Fantasy Resonance, which is out today. The game launches in October.

LEGO PlayStation confirmed

The LEGO PlayStation that leaked earlier this week was confirmed at State of Play with an official look at the PS1. The nearly 1:1 scale reproduction of the original 1994 console features 1,911 pieces and is due out later this year.

Crimson Desert DLC announced

Pearl Abyss showed Crimson Desert DLC, called Chartering the Unknown. The trailer showed off plenty of new content and systems, including what looks like a base building mechanic. Why not? Crimson Desert has pretty much every other video game system! There's also what looks like underwater exploration, Chartering the Unknown comes out October 15, 2026.

Maneater 2 announced

State of Play delivered the surprise announcement of Maneater 2! It's due out in 2027.

Metro 2039 PS5 Pro gameplay and release date

4A Games revealed a first look at upcoming shooter Metro 2039 running on PS5 Pro. The game looked fantastic in the footage shown during State of Play, with an impressive level of detail and atmospheric lighting throughout the creepy gameplay. Eventually the shooting starts, and we see the protagonist fight against a number of human enemies in a building. Outside, a storm is brewing, and the player seeks cover before it breaks. We also got a release date reveal: Metro 2039 is out February 4, 2027.

Monster Hunter Wilds expansion Ascendance

State of Play treated Monster Hunter fans to a look at Wilds expansion Ascendance, due out in 2027.

Ghost of Yotei Most Wanted

Sucker Punch showed off Ghost of Yotei Most Wanted, the upcoming single-player combat-survival roguelike mode included in the Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition, launching on October 1, 2026, for PlayStation 5. The footage showed the return of upcoming single-player combat-survival roguelike mode included in the Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition, launching on October 1, 2026, for PlayStation 5.

The footage ended with a look at Jin Sakai, the main playable character in Ghost of Tsushima. He's playable in Ghost of Yotei via Most Wanted.

Marvel's Wolverine

Sony issued one last look at Marvel's Wolverine, which is out this month exclusively on PS5. The trailer shows Wolverine fighting Trask's Sentinels as well as co-op gameplay with Sabretooth. The trailer ends with the heroes fighting an enormous Sentinel as they hunt for Trask himself.

Zach Cregger's Resident Evil

State of Play kicked off with a fresh look at Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie. The clip shown is the much talked about scene in which zombies fall from rooftops onto the street as star Austin Abrams runs for his life. This is the scene Cregger said Abrams almost died from a falling zombie!

Cregger also popped up with a message to fans. Cregger's Resident Evil hits theaters September 18, 2026.

10 minutes to go!

We're less than 10 minutes away from Sony's State of Play broadcast. Follow along with us for live updates right here.

30 minutes to go!

30 minutes until State of Play kicks off, and already people are spamming the livestream chat with #WeWantDestiny. Given what's going on with extraction shooter Marathon and developer Bungie's abandonment of Destiny 2, it probably comes as little surprise to see Destiny fans mobilize around this State of Play broadcast. The thing is, it feels extremely unlikely that Sony will green light a Destiny 3, which would surely be yet another risky expensive development project at this point. But could Bungie have more Destiny in some shape or form in the works? With Marathon struggling for player numbers, how long will Sony give it before the axe falls on that game, too?

Saros update

Housemarque's Saros is getting a free update called Zenith.

PS Plus updates

items.title: Confirmed: No Generative AI in Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 3
items.description: Following the backlash to Rideshare Stimulator’s use of generative AI, developer Saber Interactive has reassured Warhammer 40,000 fans that the technology is not in Space Marine 3 in any way.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Following the backlash to Rideshare Stimulator’s use of generative AI, developer Saber Interactive has reassured Warhammer 40,000 fans that the technology is not in Space Marine 3 in any way.

Fans of Space Marine 2 had expressed concern about the hotly-anticipated Space Marine 3 and AI when Saber confirmed generative AI had been used to develop Rideshare Stimulator, including speech and text in its Free Ride mode.

Amid the controversy, Saber CEO Matthew Karch became embroiled in a public back-and-forth with former Rideshare Stimulator writer Stella Sacco, who stated that she had been "replaced" by ChatGPT after her departure from the project in 2023 — a claim Karch denied.

"My PR team is always terrified by even broaching the subject but I would be happy to engage in a reasonable conversation about how AI can and should help shape gamer experiences," Karch told IGN at the time. "It's not and has never been about efficiencies and team reductions. Rather it's about how AI can improve the game experience.

The incident left the Steam forum for Rideshare Stimulator packed with complaints, with many calling for an AI disclosure on Valve's platform. Steam policy requires developers to report visible and in-game AI, but not background tools. An AI message was eventually added.

The Rideshare Stimulator controversy spilled over into the Space Marine community, where fans of Space Marine and Space Marine 2 — the latter an enormous hit for both Warhammer 40,000 owner Games Workshop and Saber Interactive — let their feelings be known.

“Space Marine 3 is f***ed,” said redditor Curious-Research-559 while quoting Karch in a Space Marine subreddit thread upvoted 2,800 times.

“I used to say Games Workshop is too controlling of Saber and of the Space Marine games,” added PacoThePersian. “Maybe I was judging too hastily.”

“I really hope GW threatens him with a stick or something,” said TardyTech4428. “AFAIK they are very against using AI in 40k projects and I hope they keep it that way.”

That last line is indeed true. In January, Games Workshop banned the use of AI in its content production and design process, insisting that none of its senior managers were currently excited about the technology. Then, in July, Games Workshop reiterated its anti-AI stance, and revealed it had launched investigations into recent marketing gaffes that some suspected were AI, to ensure staff were playing by internal rules.

“As noted in our November 2025 half year report, we are not being complacent on the topic, we are carefully monitoring what others are saying and doing,” Games Workshop CEO Kevin Rountree said at the time.

“We are not using AI at Games Workshop in our product design nor on the creation of our IP, this will protect the integrity and ownership of our IP. We have made a few human errors on the depiction of our products in our product marketing in the year, they were investigated fully to ensure that AI had not been used and that all our staff are following our internal policies.”

So, during an interview with Saber development chief Tim Willits at gamescom, I wanted to find out what, exactly, was being done with generative AI at Saber, and came away with confirmation that it is not being used for Space Marine 3’s development at all. Indeed, Willits promised generative AI wouldn't be found in any of Saber’s licensed titles, including Hellraiser: Revival, Stuntman: Hollywood, and Jurassic Park: Survival.

“There is absolutely no generative AI in Space Marine 3 or Hellraiser or Stuntman or Turok or Jurassic Park, or Wick,” Willits said. “But like we said, we're going to experiment with it. Try it out in Rideshare, see if it works. See if people like it. If they don't like it, we're like, ‘All right.’

“It's a rideshare simulator,” Willits continued, saying some of Saber's games are appropriate for this sort of experimentation while others are not. “If you're going to experiment, it's a good one to experiment on. You know what I'm saying?”

When I pointed out Games Workshop’s anti-AI stance, Willits said Saber follows the lead of each license owner it works with, such as Lionsgate, Universal, and Paramount. But, on Space Marine 3 specifically, I wanted to make the AI situation extra clear. “We're good,” Willits said.

So, no generative AI in Space Marine 3, which means no AI-generated dialogue, no AI-generated voices, and no AI-generated artwork. That will be good news for Warhammer 40,000’s very, very vocal fanbase, which keeps a close eye on official artwork in particular for any trace of AI use.

Still, Willits sounded, in general, interested in the potential of AI in development, which he believes has yet to be properly figured out. “If anyone tells you that they have it figured out, they don't,” he insisted. “It'll take a couple years and things will settle out and we'll figure it out.”

“We've always been using AI in some stretch of the imagination, but we as in developers, we don't really know what to do with it. Honestly, we don't,” Willits said. “If anyone tells you they do, they don't. And then players, they don't really know what to do with it. So I do believe this is going to happen. Somebody — I don't know who — somebody will come up with a game that is so freaking cool that it will change everyone's opinion and it'll be like, ‘Oh, that's it.’ And then things will settle.

“And we're still trying to figure it out. We don't have any answers. We're guessing, to be honest. But we're doing some experimentation. We'll see if it works out, doesn't work out.”

There’s no release window for Space Marine 3, but it’s deep in development at Saber Interactive as we speak. Space Marine 2, meanwhile, is still going strong with a third year of DLC support set to kick off soon.

items.title: Sony Says It Won't Pass Tariff Refunds Back to PlayStation Customers, and Dismisses Fan Arguments as 'Speculative and Illogical'
items.description: Sony has dismissed calls to return some of the $500 million it will receive in tariff refunds, despite having already passed its extra costs onto consumers through console price rises.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Sony has dismissed calls from PS5 owners to return some of the $500 million it will receive in tariff refunds, despite having already passed its extra costs onto consumers through console price rises.

The PlayStation maker has said it expects to recoup around half a billion dollars from the U.S. government, with the majority of this amount flowing back into its gaming division.

Some PS5 owners say Sony should now return some of this windfall back to them, as the company has effectively now been paid twice — in the returned tariffs, and in the extra money it charged consumers following PS5 price rises, made during the era of tariffs to ensure it didn't lose its profit margins.

Sony is far from the only company in this position, with Nintendo and Microsoft previously being pushed by fans to do the same. (Panic, the maker of indie handheld Playdate, has said it will do so, however.)

Now, in a response to legal action attempting to force Sony to hand back some of the money, the PlayStation maker has made similar arguments to those companies, and said that its customers made their own decision to buy a PS5 console at the stated price. In other words: no one was forcing them to do so, and the consoles were sold at the price that was advertised.

"Paying fair market price for voluntarily purchased consumer goods is not a legally cognizable injury," Sony's lawyers argued in a legal motion reported by Game File.

In August, Microsoft's own lawyers stated similar: "There is nothing unjust about Plaintiff purchasing an Xbox at an advertised price and getting exactly what he paid for — regardless of whatever theory he devised months later about Microsoft's cost structure."

Now, Sony is also now pushing back on what it has described as the "speculative and illogical" argument that its PS5 price hikes around the time of the tariffs were specifically caused by the tariffs. Instead, Sony has attempted to argue, its price rises were the product of a larger combination of factors, such as "inflation, currency fluctuations, component costs, logistics, competitive dynamics, or demand."

Going even further, Sony has argued that its most recent PS5 price rise is actually evidence of this in practice, as it came after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled the tariffs were illegal.

"If tariffs were the cause of the price increases, one would expect [PlayStation] to lower prices once the tariffs were eliminated — not raise them again. Instead, the timeline confirms that the pricing of PlayStation consoles includes a diverse and dynamic set of input costs."

In other words, Sony is saying that its decision to charge PS5 customers more money is proof that it needed to charge PS5 customers more money — an argument that will be interesting to see ruled on by a judge.

items.title: Spider-Man Star Andrew Garfield Hasn't Yet Congratulated Tom Holland on Brand New Day's Success, Admits He Hasn't Seen It
items.description: Andrew Garfield has admitted he's yet to congratulate Tom Holland on the incredible success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and still hasn't seen the movie.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Andrew Garfield has admitted he's yet to congratulate Tom Holland on the incredible success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and still hasn't seen the movie.

Asked by Variety whether he had checked in with his fellow Spider-bro following Brand New Day's astonishing $2.3 billion box office bonanza, Garfield said he had not, and added that he didn't want his praise to be "disingenuous."

"I don't want to be disingenuous," Garfield said. "A movie making money and people going to see it is an incredible thing, but I will reach out to him once I've seen the movie, which I'm very excited to see. And his other film, The Odyssey, I haven't managed to see either yet. I will send him a message when I see the work he has done."

Hopefully the two blockbusters meet Garfield's expectations whenever he does get around to watching them.

Meanwhile, Holland is having arguably the biggest year of his career so far, with Brand New Day breaking franchise records and now the highest-grossing film of the year so far. And, of course, it comes just after his role in Christopher Nolan's widely-praised The Odyssey, which itself has passed the $1.5 billion box office mark.

Garfield will soon be back on the big screen himself in The Uprising, a film about the 1381 Peasant's Revolt in England (which, amusingly, also stars Tom Hollander). With just a week from launch, there's been notable confusion over whether the movie is a Robin Hood origin tale or not, with U.S. and U.K. distribution companies seemingly at odds with each other on how to market the movie.

During the same interview, Garfield was asked the inevitable question of whether he would appear alongside the many dozens of other Marvel actors in Avengers: Doomsday. There have been strong rumors that Tobey Maguire's Spider-Man may put in another appearance, and the end of Doomsday appeared to suggest another Spider-Man could appear in an intergalactic (or multiversal) setting.

"No, no, I'm not. I'm not. I'm not," was Garfield's response. "You'll find out, I suppose, one way or the other."

Image credit: Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images.

items.title: Planet Coaster Maker Announces Disney Game Development, Opening Doors to a Disneyland Park Creator
items.description: Frontier Developments, the studio behind Jurassic World Evolution, Planet Zoo, and Planet Coaster, has inked a deal with Disney to develop an upcoming game.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Frontier Developments, the studio behind Jurassic World Evolution, Planet Zoo, and Planet Coaster, has inked a deal with Disney to develop an upcoming game.

While details of the project remain thin on the ground for now, a press release sent to IGN stated that the game will "build upon the company's extensive experience and proven capabilities as a leader in the creative management simulation genre." In other words, expect a Disney sim game.

It's not a huge leap to expect something akin to a Disneyland park creator, especially as the studio is well versed in extending its expertise to licensed properties via its Jurassic World Evolution franchise. Indeed, Frontier made 2011's Kinect: Disneyland Adventures, which was eventually remastered and made playable without Kinect.

"We are delighted to announce this collaboration with Disney, which further reinforces our clearly defined strategy of developing and nurturing world-class creative management simulation game franchises," noted Frontier CEO Jo Cooke.

"Our mission with this game is to connect a passionate creative community of players with one of the world's most iconic and beloved brands, and I can't wait to see what our talented teams will create with this amazing opportunity."

As well as its freshly-inked Disney deal, the studio reaffirmed today that it also has another unannounced Planet sim game in the works. Planet Zoo 2 launches in October, and Frontier is set to publish strategy game Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate – Deathwatch.

Image credit: AaronP/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images.

items.title: Resident Evil's Zach Cregger Admits He Was 'Naive' to Assume Fans Would Approve of Him Avoiding a Direct Adaptation of the Games
items.description: Zach Cregger admitted that he was “naive” to think his less-direct approach to adapting Resident Evil would be universally well-received by fans after deliberately choosing to avoid retelling the story exactly as it unfolds in the games.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Zach Cregger admitted that he was “naive” to think his less-direct approach to adapting Resident Evil would be universally well-received by fans after deliberately choosing to avoid retelling the story exactly as it unfolds in the games.

Cregger’s Resident Evil movie follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who gets caught up in the madness of the Raccoon City Incident. The writer/director confirmed previously that this film takes place in parallel to the events of Resident Evil 2 and that it focuses more on what it feels like as a player to navigate through zombie-filled corridors and sneak around Lickers… but not everyone was anticipating an original story told within the continuity of Capcom’s beloved horror game franchise.

Instead, a slew of fans have lashed out at Cregger for not directly adapting an existing game in the series, with many arguing that, without characters like Leon, Ada, and Jill, this isn’t really a Resident Evil movie at all.

IGN’s Tom Jorgensen got the chance to sit down with Cregger to ask him about his feelings on this particular topic — and his response was strikingly self-aware.

“I think I was naive,” he said. “I thought fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie. I was like, ‘That’s great.’ I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing. I get it, I understand the frustration. I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?

“My only hope is that they’ll see the movie regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment that I’m not telling some of the stories that the games tell so well, and they will feel seen when they do watch the movie, and they will recognize all of the love for the games that are in this movie, because it is there. This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story. I understand the resistance, I do, because I have it myself. It is coming from a true place of love.”

Cregger’s love for the Resident Evil series is evident in multiple references that have been included in his movie, a few of which fans have already seen in the trailers. For instance, we get to see Austin Abrams rummaging through drawers and closets looking for bullets for a shotgun he pilfered (Heavy Ammo Shotgun Shells), running into padlocks that impede his progress, and, of course, a typewriter sitting in what appears to be a safe room.

More recently, we got a promotional poster for the film with a delivery slip detailing an organ transplant to Umbrella Corp, confirming that the shadowy biotech group is involved in Cregger’s movie. A teaser on social media also showed off a few first-person action sequences that hearken back to Resident Evil 7 and 8.

Cregger previously spoke on fans’ reactions to the movie with IGN at San Diego Comic-Con, where he admitted that he “took liberties” with his adaptation and explained why he chose not to make one-to-one adaptations of existing games in the series.

“The games are so well executed, and to me, Leon and Claire and these characters, they exist so perfectly in the games that anyone I cast and any difference that I do with them would be, probably, to the detriment of what I was trying to do,” he told us.

Resident Evil releases in theaters on September 18, 2026.

items.title: The Witcher 4, Cyberpunk 2077 Developer CD Projekt Red Ramps Up Hiring on 'Project Hadar'
items.description: The Witcher and Cyberpunk developer CD Projekt Red is staffing up for its unannounced 'Project Hadar', as that team is currently over 30 people strong with plans "to hire more, up to 50 developers by the end of this year," CD Projekt Red vice president of investor relations Karolina Gnas said on the company latest earnings call on Wednesday.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
The Witcher and Cyberpunk developer CD Projekt Red is staffing up for its unannounced 'Project Hadar', as that team is currently over 30 people strong with plans "to hire more, up to 50 developers by the end of this year," CD Projekt Red vice president of investor relations Karolina Gnas said on the company latest earnings call on Wednesday. The Project Hadar news was first reported by GamesRadar.

"Right now, the team is mostly focused on testing different approaches, ideas, and, you know, prototyping some gameplay element, and this is it," Gnas added. "Hadar is still in the concept phase." CDPR also confirmed that the remake of The Witcher 1 is on hold in favor of putting more resources into The Witcher 4, which the studio is targeting for a 2028 release, as well as the just-announced decade-later Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past.

But what is Project Hadar? It's tough to guess at this point, as The Witcher is a third-person fantasy RPG, while Cyberpunk is a first-person RPG shooter. Hadar being an RPG of some caliber is the only reasonably safe bet at this point.

Regardless, CDPR is nothing if not busy, with The Witcher 3 Remastered due out this month (and thankfully, existing owners get upgraded free and, yes, your old save files will work), plus The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, The Witcher 4, a Cyberpunk sequel, the aforementioned Witcher 1 remake, and Project Hadar all in development.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Over 600 Unused Voice Lines From Resident Evil 4 Leak Online, Showing That Capcom Intended to Connect the Game to Village
items.description: Over 30 minutes’ worth of unused voice lines from Resident Evil 4 Remake have surfaced online, one of which proves that Capcom wanted to make a connection to Village.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Ovee 30 minutes’ worth of unused voice lines from Resident Evil 4 Remake have surfaced online, one of which proves that Capcom wanted to make a connection to Village.

This leak comes from a notable community modder named Keff0, who uncovered both audio and subtitles for a whopping 671 lines on the game’s PlayStation 5 launch disc. These lines aren’t on the PC version of the game, and they’re fully recorded, featuring dialogue from Leon, Luis, Ashley, and the Merchant.

One of the Merchant’s unused lines is standing out to viewers, as he mentions a character that wasn’t even a blink in the RE Team’s mind when the game was first made back in the mid-2000s.

“Ah, I see you’re no stranger to villages. The Duke? Lad shows promise,” the Merchant says.

Resident Evil fans will make the connection to the series’ eighth game, Village, which features another merchant character who simply calls himself ‘The Duke.’ Funny enough, The Duke also references the Resident Evil 4 merchant as players browse through his wares, saying, “‘What’re ya buyin’?’ Haha, just something an old friend of mine used to say.”

Capcom’s decision to cut The Merchant’s line from RE4 Remake is a bit saddening, as it would have further cemented the relationship between these characters and added a bit more continuity to the timeline, if retroactively. However, this insertion of a modern-day Resident Evil character in the series’ single-most beloved game could have rubbed some players the wrong way, though we’ll never know for certain why Capcom chose to leave this particular dialogue out of the final product.

😮Over 600 cut voice lines have been found in Resident Evil 4 Remake.

Modder Keff0, who previously restored the game’s cut Chapter 0 and made it playable, has now uncovered 671 finished voice lines that were cut from Resident Evil 4 Remake.

🔎All of the lines can be found on… pic.twitter.com/obSogcJG6t

— RENEWS (@RENews_X) September 1, 2026

This wasn’t the only interesting find from the RE4 Remake; Keff0 also uncovered unused animations for the Merchant’s death, meaning that originally, players would have been able kill him. His shop was even supposed to close after he died, and save data found by Keff0 shows that he’d be gone for the rest of the game. This would have made it more similar to the original, but it seems like the team at Capcom thought that’d be too counterintuitive to this modern rework of the title.

Like many AAA games, there’s a swath of unused lines, scenes, art, enemies, characters, and other assets in recent Resident Evil titles that don’t make it to the final cut; earlier this year, Leon’s voice actor revealed that his favorite line in Resident Evil Requiem was ultimately axed by Capcom — and it’s a shame, because it was hilarious.

Luckily, there’s much more to come, with Code Veronica getting a remake in 2027 and a live-action Resident Evil movie directed by Zach Cregger set to hit theaters this month.

items.title: The Witcher Remake Is on Hold Until The Witcher 4's Development Progresses, Confirms CD Projekt Red
items.description: The remake of The Witcher is currently on hold while the team focuses on The Witcher 4 and The Witcher 3's new expansion, according to CD Projekt Red.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The remake of The Witcher is currently on hold while the team focuses on The Witcher 4 and The Witcher 3's new expansion, according to CD Projekt Red.

Developer Fool's Theory is helping out on The Witcher 4 and developing The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion, but it is also attached to remake the first Witcher game. Unfortunately, that remake is on the hold for the time being. The studio confirmed this in a statement to GameSpot, noting that part of the hold up is due to the fact that the remake is being built on the back of The Witcher 4. As a result, the development team working on the remake will have to wait until The Witcher 4 gets further into development so that the remake can utilize all of the assets and tools created for the next installment.

“Fool’s Theory team is focused mainly on the development of Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, while a relatively small part of their team is supporting the development of The Witcher 4," said a CDPR rep. "As we have previously announced, the development on The Witcher Remake has been temporarily integrated with The Witcher 4 due to production process dependencies. As The Witcher Remake will be built on the foundation laid by The Witcher 4, we need to have the necessary assets, tools, and pipelines ready for efficient development.”

All in all, it doesn't sound like there's any reason to be concerned about whether The Witcher remake will see the light of day. Fool's Theory appears to be working on The Witcher 4 specifically so it can get familiar with the new tools and processes before continuing development on the remake. The Witcher remake was announced in 2022, and the team has openly talked about how it will be an open-world game that will remove or remake parts of the original that they feel are outdated or bad.

Ultimately, it sounds like we shouldn't expect The Witcher remake before 2028. CD Projekt Red has stated The Witcher 4 is currently slated to arrive in 2028, and it plans to complete a trilogy within six years of The Witcher 4's debut. It seems like the remake of The Witcher could come between The Witcher 4 and 5 to help keep fans busy.

CD Projekt Red is also developing a plethora of other projects, including a new IP, currently codenamed Project Hadar. Not much is known about the title, but CDPR confirmed today that it is ramping up hiring on the project while prototyping the game.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

"With voice actors, particularly with voice actors who do main character roles, it is a reality that people are ripping our voices off. That's happening. It's happened to me on multiple occasions. Every time somebody does that, they're effectively robbing me of income, and not just me, any other voice actor who they do it with. We're all watching our voices get used in ways that we would rather they weren't. Somebody could use AI to produce something racist using Geralt's voice, using my voice, or just something against anything that most normal people think is good. That's where the AI gets dangerous. Fake news, false news, false opinions. We're seeing it with politicians now. People are putting things out there. So AI is not the problem. It's the people using AI." Speaking to IGN.

items.title: TimTheTatman Turned Down Six-Figure Deal to Stream Arc Raiders Because He Hates It So Much
items.description: TimTheTatman has revealed that he turned down an eye-watering amount of money for a sponsored Arc Raiders stream.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
TimTheTatman has revealed that he turned down an eye-watering amount of money for a sponsored Arc Raiders stream.

The streamer was speaking candidly to his audience during a September 2 broadcast when he revealed that he'd turned down a six-figure deal to play Arc Raiders on stream for four hours. While the exact dollar amount is unknown, hundreds of thousands of dollars to play a game for an afternoon is an absolutely baffling amount of money. TimTheTatman stated that he had such an unpleasant experience with the game that even a jaw-dropping amount of cash couldn't bring him back.

"For me, the game frustrated me so much, I got frustrated so much with that game that I don't want to play it ever again," he said. "Even to a point where six figures didn't get me back on it."

TimTheTatman explains why he turned down a 6 figure ad deal to stream Arc Raiders for 4 hours.

“For me that game frustrated me so much that I never want to play it again. To a point where six figures couldn't get me back on it." pic.twitter.com/Ws8qyO6ye2

— ModernWarzone (@ModernWarzone) September 2, 2026

He joked that a seven-figure deal would be enough to make him get over his frustrations and play the game, but ultimately, it's not an experience he wants to revisit. Arc Raiders was one of the biggest games of 2025, but it has gradually declined over the last year. The game launched in a hyper-competitive window alongside the likes of Battlefield 6 and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, but managed to capture a strong, supportive fan base at launch.

The game peaked with 465,000 concurrents on Steam in December 2025, two months after release, but things began to decline shortly after this. Arc Raiders players began to complain about a lack of meaningful new content and updates, causing players to lose interest. Eventually, Embark Studios confirmed that Arc Raiders would only get two major updates a year going forward and unfortunately, the studio just recently delayed future expeditions until 2027.

Naturally, some fans just aren't happy with the state of Arc Raiders. That lack of interest seems to be rubbing off on content creators who can't even muster some fake enthusiasm for a paycheck, it seems.

Ikea is partnering up with Skyrim in an unexpected collaboration that has fans making the same joke about The Elder Scrolls 6.

On September 2, the official Ikea accounts for Ireland and the United Kingdom posted a promotional video on Instagram, showing a mountain of familiar Skyrim memorabilia haphazardly tossed onto a snowy mountainside… alongside some comparatively modern-looking pieces.

For instance, a rune-inscribed Allen wrench is stuffed amongst the frozen Nord helmets, pots, swords, books, and wheels of cheese, while a white Kallax 4x2 shelf sits on top of the pile.

A date is then shown: September 9, 2026, along with the message, “Coming to the Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.” The post’s caption says much the same thing: “A Creation coming to The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.”

Thus far, it’s unclear exactly what this collaboration entails. Does this mean that the Kallax shelf will be available for players to decorate their homes with? Will they be able to use the magic Allen wrench as a weapon? (That would be hilarious.) Or is furniture from the game coming to IKEA?

Either way, fans are all saying the same thing: We’re getting an Ikea collab, of all things, before The Elder Scrolls 6 comes out.

“New Elder Scrolls? No. New Skyrim furniture that will break down before the new Elder Scrolls comes out? Yes,” one user wrote on X.

“Heard they're reforming the Dawnguard. Vampire hunters or something, in the old IKEA near Riften. Might consider joining up, myself,” another joked on Instagram.

It seems like Ikea is moving full speed ahead into the gaming market, having recently announced a furniture line catering specifically to gamers. Titled The Yxstaby Collection, this furniture line was first shown off at gamescom this year, with pieces inspired by the Xbox controller.

It includes a TV stand, a side table, a ‘thumbstick’ stool, a D-pad cushion and platter, a lounge chair, and more. IGN even got the chance to speak with Carl Ledbetter, Xbox's Head of Design, at Gamescom, where he opened up about the brand's inspiration for the collaboration.

"I’ve spent all my time [at Xbox] looking at input, controllers, the console, how things fit into the home. [That] matters when you design a console, [the] horizontal and vertical position. [So] this goes back years. The philosophy that we share for designing products at Xbox and at Ikea are nearly identical. So it was like a love connection," he told us.

For now, fans’ll just have to wait for more information on The Elder Scrolls 6, which recently got a big update after Xbox CEO Asha Sharma publicly declared that she saw an early playthrough of the game in August, calling the scale and grandeur “incredible” and the story “even greater."

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Kat Dennings Recalls Her Six-Hour Mad Max: Fury Road Audition With 'Wonderful Person' Tom Hardy
items.description: Kat Dennings shared the heartwarming details of her Mad Max: Fury Road audition with Tom Hardy, revealing how a grueling screen test took a sweet turn in the end.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
2 Broke Girls and WandaVision actress Kat Dennings took to social media to recall her experience auditioning opposite Tom Hardy for 2015's Mad Max: Fury Road. Although Dennings at one point likens the audition to being like “an acting class if it was [on] the worst day of your life,” her story ultimately takes a surprisingly sweet and funny turn.

Dennings explained on TikTok how her screen test – she doesn’t specify which role she was up for but presumably it was for one of Immortan Joe’s Brides – took an epic six hours. It was a chemistry read between her and Hardy, who, of course, went on to win the title role of "Mad Max" Rockatansky.

Dennings, who still lived at home with her parents at the time, said director George Miller didn’t do much talking during the audition, with a person she believes was an acting coach leading the process instead.

@katdenningsss

With a twist at the end

♬ Quirky Suspenseful Indie-Comedy(1115050) - Kenji Ueda

“The dialogue was a couple of pages, and kind of vague. And basically, what happened was, an acting class, if it was, um, the worst day of your life. At one point, they had us switch roles. They had the camera and had us like running around the corner,” Dennings said.

“The worst part of it, I do believe, was when the acting coach told us to say the lines without saying the lines, encouraging us to just make noises instead of the lines. I was dying. I mean, Tom Hardy, he really took to this exercise. Like, he was able to be extremely free and come up with very creative ways of doing these lines.”

Dennings said “the best part of the story” is its ending and she’s absolutely right.

After the audition was finally over after six grueling hours, Dennings – who didn’t have a car – planned to go down the corner to call for a ride, but Hardy then offered to give her a lift.

“He drove me home. He was so lovely. We get to my house, which was my parents' house, because I still lived at home with my parents. And he came inside and he met my mom, and he was like, oh, what a nice house. She was like, oh, come on in. And I was like, all right, Tom, well, this is a very special day. Uh, I hope, uh, you move further in this experience because I know that I'm not going to. I went back to the converted garage where I lived, put my pajamas on, took a nap. A few hours later, I go back into the main house, and Tom Hardy is still there. Having tea with my mother, and just chatting it up. So... I can't say enough about Tom Hardy. I will be a fan of his for life. I think he's a wonderful person, and my mom still talks about him.”

While Dennings didn’t land a role in Mad Max: Fury Road, she did join the MCU as Darcy Lewis in the Thor films.

Hardy, you may have heard, just dropped a rap album he collaborated on with Czarface where, under the alias Frankie Pulitzer, he raps about everything from Willem Dafoe’s Green Goblin to Kathy Bates.

items.title: Sony Is Making 59% More Revenue Per PlayStation User Since PS4 Generation, Says Analyst
items.description: Sony is making 59% more money per active PlayStation user now than they were during the PS4 era, according to new data compiled by Niko Partners Director of Research and Insights Daniel Ahmad, who covers the video game market with a focus on the Asia and MENA markets. It translates to $230 more spent by the average active PlayStation user now than in 2018.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Sony is making 59% more money per active PlayStation user now than they were during the PS4 era, according to new data compiled by Niko Partners Director of Research and Insights Daniel Ahmad, who covers the video game market with a focus on the Asia and MENA markets. It translates to $230 more spent by the average active PlayStation user now than in 2018.

Responding to a new interview with Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki duscussing why the company isn't as aggressive in marketing the PS5 these days, Ahmad took to X to post, "I did the math on this and average annual revenue per PlayStation active user has grown from 23,580 Yen in FY2018 to 37,485 Yen in FY2025, which is around $230. [It's] an increase of 59% over that period. Although growth was flat over the past year or two."

For more detail and context, he added, "FY19 includes through to March 2020, with Covid leading to a boost in active users. Main drivers here are the transition to higher PS+ tiers, higher spending on game software and DLC / MTX, higher prices for hardware, etc." In short, Ahmad seems to suggest that Sony doesn't need to spend as much money to aggressively market the PS5, in the face of its and every console's rising prices, because it's making more money off of the users it already has.

Sony remains under fire from many gamers who are unsatisfied with the company's new physical games policy, which will see the company stop offering disc-based copies of games in January of 2028. Microsoft, meanwhile, is offering its Xbox players the chance to digitize their disc-based Xbox games as its next-gen Project Helix console/PC hybrid device approaches.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: A Playable Build of an Unreleased Scream Game Has Surfaced Thanks to the Steam Leak
items.description: An unreleased Scream game has found its way online thanks to the recent Steam leak.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
An unreleased Scream game has found its way online thanks to the recent Steam leak.

Last week, Steam was hit with a massive leak that saw tons of files and builds from the years 2003–2013 dumped online. It's been an interesting treasure trove for those who like gaming history, but one of the most unexpected things to come out of the incident is a playable build for a licensed Scream game that was never announced or released.

Kotaku spotted X / Twitter user roly poly reaper talking about the game and sharing never-before-seen gameplay.

update: we got multiplayer to work using goldberg emu + radmin VPN. heres footage of it running in the final build of the game pic.twitter.com/CpWOF9Y7RP

— roly poly reaper (@fellarobux) August 31, 2026

Interestingly enough, the game appears to be very similar to the likes of Dead by Daylight. One player would fill the shoes of Ghostface and track down ordinary players who are trying to collect evidence against the killer. The game was in the works from a developer known as Fatshark and would've predated Dead by Daylight and the Friday the 13th games, meaning it was a bit ahead of its time.

It's unclear exactly when this was developed, but it wouldn't be surprising if this took place around the time of Scream 4 in 2011. The franchise had been on ice for a decade prior to that film, so it would make sense if the rights owners were trying to generate some brand synergy. While we'll never get to play the finished version of this Scream game, some of the fans digging through the files were able to get multiplayer working.

It's an interesting relic from the past and one that would probably make more sense these days, should Paramount Games be interested in taking another crack at things. Dead by Daylight is still a huge title, and later this week, Halloween: The Game will release for early access owners. Whether that one sticks the landing remains to be seen, but previews have been pretty positive so far.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.
